remaining_concerns: No new admissible evidence was added; the Actor reframed the same weak record.

The narrowed rationale is better bounded, but the core compliance predicate remains only partially supported: the summary still does not clearly establish that the unresolved issues crossed the policy threshold to a material unresolved risk requiring rejection rather than follow-up or temporary hold.
BPROC-044-E, as summarized, supports blocking approval pending follow-up if storage controls remained unresolved, but that is not the same as clear admissible support for a reject-level outcome.
The Actor concedes there is no formally logged control failure and no explicit materiality threshold memo in the record.
Because evidence access is limited to the Actor's summary, the overstatement risk remains if the rejection is labeled cleanly compliant rather than caveated or escalated.
final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor provided no new admissible evidence and instead offered a narrower interpretation of the same cited items. That reinterpretation improves the framing: it avoids claiming a definitive control failure and limits the justification to unresolved diligence risk at award time. But the distinction matters. A caveated, policy-bounded position can support compliant_with_caveats only if the caveat does not leave the central compliance predicate unresolved. Here, it still does. The policy requires admissible evidence of a material unresolved risk for rejection. On the available summary, the cited quality-process gap, prior quality lapse, and questionnaire inconsistency mainly support follow-up or escalation; BPROC-044-E appears to strengthen that unresolved issues should block approval pending follow-up, but it still does not clearly convert the record into a reject-level showing. So the packet is narrower and more defensible than the original overbroad claim, but it remains overstated relative to what the admissible summary clearly proves. Business-cost arguments are not evidence and do not affect the audit outcome.
